newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha softer, backwardation shrinks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha softer, backwardation shrinks.

text.p: Naphtha prices declined in Tokyo trade on Tuesday, in line with a sharp fall in overnight crude prices, while the backwardation in near-term naphtha spreads narrowed for the first time in a week, traders said.
"Today's naphtha kept pace with crude," one trader said.
On Monday, naphtha prices held ground in the Tokyo market despite overnight crude losses, reflecting healthy fundamentals.
Open-specification naphtha for second-half April was assessed at $231.00/233.00 per tonne, shedding about $5.50 from late Monday dealing.
First-half May was offered at $229.00, while no bids emerged. It was traded once at $234.00, and again at $233.50 on Monday.
Second-half May was quoted at around $225.00/226.00 after it was sold from a Japanese trader to a European trading house at $225.00 in Tuesday afternoon trade.

Naphtha's inter-month spreads narrowed substantially as sellers came down with their offer prices amid a lack of firm buyers. Second-half April/second-half May was indicated at plus $6.00/7.00, down from Monday's $8.00/9.00.
